bug_info.bug_desc: When a PMP error occurs during a load operation, lsu_resp_valid_o is asserted based on pmp_err_q being high while the FSM is in IDLE state. This causes lsu_rdata_valid_o to also be asserted (since it's derived from lsu_resp_valid_o & ~data_we_q), which incorrectly signals the register file to write back data. The issue is that pmp_err_q alone should not trigger a valid response when no actual memory transaction has completed—the response should only be valid when data_rvalid_i is asserted (indicating a real memory response) or when the error condition is properly qualified with the transaction state.
bug_info.fix_hint: Qualify `lsu_rdata_valid_o` with an actual `data_rvalid_i` response in the IDLE completion state, require a load operation, and suppress it for data or PMP errors so error responses cannot enable register writeback.
